title: Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans: Grace Period and Notice Periods Scheduled by Plan
content:
Three periods, all counted in calendar days, are scheduled per plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans: the days allowed after a first unpaid contribution before a disenrollment may be processed, the days of notice a sponsor must give to end its group contract, and the days of notice retirees receive when the sponsor ends that contract.

| Group plan | Contribution grace period | Sponsor notice to end the group contract | Retiree notice on group termination |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Standard (PPO) | 60 | 90 | 60 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Enhanced (PPO) | 60 | 90 | 60 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Premium (PPO) | 90 | 120 | 90 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Standard (EGWP) | 60 | 90 | 60 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Enhanced (EGWP) | 60 | 90 | 60 |
| Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Premium (EGWP) | 90 | 120 | 90 |

## Reading of the timetable

The longer scale stands on Ridgecrest Group Retiree Premium (PPO) and Ridgecrest Group Retiree Rx Premium (EGWP): 90 calendar days of grace, 120 calendar days of sponsor notice and 90 calendar days of retiree notice. The remaining four plans of the book stand at 60, 90 and 60 calendar days in the same order.

On every plan of the book the notice a sponsor must give to end the group contract is the longest of the three periods, and it exceeds the notice the retirees then receive by 30 calendar days.

The grace period and the retiree notice period are equal on each plan of this book, but they are periods of different things: one runs on an unpaid contribution, the other on the ending of the group contract itself.
